text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Friday. Prepared for Reuters by the Cooperation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- A Russian embassy representative said Russia's official viewpoint on Latvia's protests over Russian warships entering Latvia's economic zone were unfounded as under international law any ship can freely navigate in economic zones.

- Latvia's foreign ministry ambassador-at-large, Aivars Vovers, said the presence of Russian ships in Latvia's economic zone without informing Latvia should be regarded as an unfriendly gesture by the Russian side.
- Parliament passed a bill on official secrets, which regulates the preservation, use and protection of state secrets.
- Parliament chose three judges for the planned constitutional court but the other seven candidates failed to collect the necessary 51 votes.
- By 57 votes against 11 and two abstentions parliament rejected a no-confidence vote against the government moved by some of the smaller parties.

- Prime Minister Andris Shkele issued a warning to deputy prime minister Ziedonis Chevers and Defence Minister Andrej Krastinsh for failing to submit documents he requested in time. Both officials said they handed over the documents and the delay was in the prime minister's own office.
- A low demand for T-bills in this week's auction provoked a rise in rates on 28-day and three-month Treasury bills.
- 38 Latvian companies took part last week in an exhibition, Expo Latvia, in the Russian city of Pskov.
